label: SEIS Seismometer & Robotic Grapple

specs.sensitivity: Measures ground motion smaller than a hydrogen atom (10⁻¹⁰ m/s²)
specs.lead_institution: CNES / IPGP (France) with ETH Zurich and Imperial College

function: Ultra-sensitive French-led seismometer deployed directly onto the Martian regolith via the robotic grapple. Detected over 1,300 marsquakes, revealing the thickness of Mars's crust and the liquid nature of its metallic core.
missionFacts: Detected the largest marsquake ever recorded on May 4, 2022 (Magnitude 4.7 lasting over 10 hours)
Confirmed that the Martian crust is between 24 and 72 km thick with at least two internal layers
Measured meteorite impacts shaking the planet and creating 150-meter fresh craters
Placed safely under a dome shield to protect sensors from violent Martian winds

label: Instrument Deployment Arm (IDA) & IDC Camera

specs.arm_reach: 1.9 m (6.2 ft) with 4 degrees of freedom
specs.camera: Instrument Deployment Camera (IDC) mounted on elbow (1024 × 1024 color)

function: Articulated robotic arm designed to grasp, lift, and place scientific instruments from the lander deck onto the Martian soil with sub-centimeter precision. Also used its scoop to pile regolith onto the HP3 mole.
missionFacts: First robotic arm in history to place free-standing instruments onto another planet's surface
Pushed down on the HP3 'mole' thermal probe with its scoop to provide traction in powdery soil
Used its scoop to trickle sand onto the lander's solar panels during wind gusts to blow away dust
Took final self-portraits before dust accumulation ended the mission in December 2022

label: UltraFlex Decagonal Solar Array Wings

specs.span: 5.98 m (19.6 ft) total wing tip-to-tip span
specs.diameter: 2.15 m (7.0 ft) per circular fan-like array
specs.power_capacity: ~600 to 700 W at landing; dropped to <100 W by mission end due to dust

function: Twin circular folding photovoltaic wings engineered by Northrop Grumman. Unfolded like Japanese paper fans after touchdown on Elysium Planitia to charge two 23-Ah lithium-ion batteries.
missionFacts: Produced 4,600 watt-hours per sol during initial deployment on Elysium Planitia
Dust storms slowly covered the arrays over 4 years, reducing power output by 85%
Engineers prolonged mission life by pulsing motors to vibrate panels and shake off dust
Operated for 1,445 sols — more than double its planned 709-sol prime mission

label: Three-Leg Landing Struts & Retrorockets

specs.leg_count: 3 landing legs with crushable honeycomb shock absorbers
specs.thrusters: 12 pulsed hydrazine descent thrusters (300 N each)

function: Tripod landing gear providing stable foundation for sensitive seismic measurements. Dissipated kinetic energy upon touchdown on November 26, 2018 at Elysium Planitia.
missionFacts: Descended through the Martian atmosphere using a supersonic parachute and 12 pulsed thrusters
Landed at Elysium Planitia with less than a 4-degree slope on a smooth, rock-free plain
The Instrument Context Camera (ICC) mounted on the front leg provided wide 124° fish-eye views
Remains stationary and silent on Elysium Planitia (4.502° N, 135.623° E)
